questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Did the employee ask the employer to state the reasons for the immediate dismissal in writing?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Did the employer end the employment relationship with immediate effect, without a notice period?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Was the employment relationship agreed for a fixed term, with an agreed end date, rather than for an unlimited period?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Has the employee earned income from other work during the time the notice period or the agreed term would still have run?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Does the employer give as the cause of the dismissal the employee's absence from work, and does the employee say they were prevented from working through no fault of their own (for instance illness, accident or a non-voluntary legal obligation)?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Does the file say that a written individual employment contract, a standard employment contract or a collective employment contract sets notice periods different from the statutory ones (seven days during probation, art. 335b para. 1; one month in the first year of service, two months in the second to ninth years, three months thereafter)?

text:
Good evening,

On 14 January 2026 the Talgrund Cooperative in Thun sacked me on the spot. Chris Huber, who runs the cooperative's workshop, phoned me at home and said I was finished as of that day, no notice period, and that my last wage would be paid only up to the 14th.

His reason was that I had 'stopped turning up'. That is true in a way: I had been away for almost three weeks. But on 23 December I was knocked off my bike by a car at the Bahnhofstrasse crossing and broke my leg in two places. I was in hospital and then at home in plaster, and I couldn't have worked if I'd wanted to. My friend Peter Baumann took the doctor's note to the workshop for me on 28 December.

As for money since then, it's a bit unclear. In early March I did two trial days at a bakery in Thun. They said they would 'sort out the pay for the trial days later', and I don't know yet whether they'll pay me for them or not. Apart from that I'm looking for work.

The annoying part is that my job had a fixed end date anyway. My contract started on 30 May 2025 and was agreed until 31 May 2026, because the cooperative needed extra hands for a building project. So I'd have had a few more months.

I didn't ask Mr Huber to put his reasons in writing. After that phone call I just didn't want to speak to him again.

My wage was CHF 2,060 a month. Can I get the wages up to the end of May?

Thank you,
Noah Carter
Bahnhofstrasse 68, Thun
